title: Scheduling fairness pulse notes (scratchpad)
content:
Goal: quick scratchpad for experiments exploring request scheduling fairness under bursty coalescence and how it interacts with KV-cache warmup. Not a final writeup — brain dump + raw numbers + next steps.

Background/context
- Motivation: observed mid-latency tail increases when a high-priority stream coexists with many small low-priority requests during coalescing windows. Suspect unfair queueing + cache thrashing.
- Hypothesis: naive coalescing (time-window based) tends to favor whatever arrival batch hits the window boundary and can starve other lanes for a short period. If KV-cache gets primed by the favored lane, subsequent requests gain advantage.

Experiment setup (lightweight)
- Single GPU local dev cluster (4x A100 sim), runtime: dev-build 2025-11-01, coalescer modes: time-window (TW), request-count (RC), adaptive (AD).
- Workload: two logical lanes: HP (high-priority, qps=50, payload ~ 32 tokens), LP (low-priority, qps=300, payload 8 tokens). Zipf alpha=1.2 for LP to simulate skew.
- Measure: p50/p95/p99 latency, qps delivered per lane, KV-cache hit rate, GPU utilization, observed batching distribution (batch sizes over time).
- Short runs: 10 minutes steady + three 2-minute microbursts (LP qps -> 1200) at T=3,6,9 minutes.

Baseline: TW window=10ms, max-batch=64
- HP p50: 18ms, p95: 46ms, p99: 110ms
- LP p50: 28ms, p95: 210ms, p99: 650ms (spikes during microbursts)
- KV-cache hit rate overall: 72% (HP: 88%, LP: 68%)
- Observations: during LP microbursts, TW coalescer creates very large batches dominated by LP; HP requests that arrive slightly after boundary get queued to next window and see high tail.

RC mode: request-count threshold=32, max-wait=5ms
- HP p50: 19ms, p95: 38ms, p99: 82ms
- LP p50: 32ms, p95: 120ms, p99: 420ms
- KV-cache overall: 69% (HP: 85%, LP: 66%)
- Observations: RC keeps batch sizes more stable, reduces extremely large batches. HP tail improves vs TW but LP still suffers during large bursts because RC saturates and creates backlog.

AD mode (adaptive: target latency 40ms, window adjusted 2-20ms)
- HP p50: 17ms, p95: 34ms, p99: 72ms
- LP p50: 30ms, p95: 95ms, p99: 290ms
- KV-cache overall: 74% (HP: 90%, LP: 71%)
- Observations: AD seems best tradeoff. It shortens windows when latency climbs, preventing one lane from monopolizing coalescing slots. LP tails still elevated but less extreme.

Fairness probe (priority inversion scenarios)
- Inject periodic HP burst (200 qps for 15s) overlapping LP sustained high qps. Run AD + per-lane max-in-flight knobs (HP cap = 40 in-flight).
- With no per-lane cap: HP bursts lead to LP starvation for 8-12s, p99(LP) > 1.2s.
- With HP cap = 40: LP p99 reduces to ~320ms, HP p99 increases modestly (from 72ms to 120ms).
- Note: cap works as crude fairness knob but causes HP partial slowdown; still acceptable for user-facing fairness policy.

KV-cache interaction notes
- When HP warms a small set of KV keys aggressively, HP enjoys persistent low latency. LP keys have lower reuse -> cache churn.
- Idea: add lane-aware KV retention hint (on-cache-insert tag with TTL bias by lane) -> make coalescing fairness translate into cache fairness. Small quick test: mark LP inserts with TTL*1.5 -> LP cache hit rose +4–6% and LP tail dropped ~10–15% in p95. Side effects: increased memory usage, needs guardrails.

Micro-observations / fragments
- Large batches dominated by tiny-token LP requests increase amortized kernel overhead but hurt HP 1-2x for p99.
- Adaptive window with per-lane slotting (reserve N slots per window for HP) looked promising in simulation: reduces HP misses while keeping LP throughput within 85% of baseline.
- Strange artifact: when switching modes during run, GPU utilization dips for ~300ms then recovers — look into worker warm-up on coalescer config reload (possible lock contention).

Next quick experiments (priority list)
1) Run AD + lane-aware KV TTL at scale (30m run) and collect memory pressure stats.
2) Try hybrid coalescer: time-window + reserved slots per lane (configurable). Short A/B against AD.
3) Per-lane max-in-flight + backpressure shaping (soft vs hard cap) — measure percent degraded HP requests.
4) Instrument per-batch composition telemetry (histogram of lane mix) and feed to optimizer to auto-adjust window/slots.

Run commands (dev notes)
- workload runner: ./tools/sim-load --config experiments/sched-fair/ad-config.yaml --out /tmp/run1
- collect: ./tools/collect-telemetry /tmp/run1 --ids batch,kv,hostmetrics --out /tmp/tele1.json
- quick plot: python tools/plot_latency.py /tmp/tele1.json --lanes HP,LP --percentiles 50,95,99

Open questions / risks
- TTL bias may cause cache amplification for rare keys; need guardrail to avoid OOM in dedicated pools.
- How to expose fairness knobs in API/console without overwhelming customers? Provide presets: conservative, balanced, aggressive-cost.
- Interplay with preemption: if we preempt long LP batches to favor HP, we risk wasted compute (partial batch work). Need graceful partial batching semantics.

Quick conclusions (working)
- Adaptive coalescing + modest per-lane caps gives best practical fairness vs raw TW/RC.
- KV-cache lane hints materially help tails for disadvantaged lanes but require memory safety checks.
- UI/automation: we should expose a "fairness profile" and collect telemetry to recommend presets.

Notes-to-self / TODOs
- Expand runs to include heterogeneous token lengths (random 8-256) next week.
- File GH PR with AD implementation notes and toggles (see linked PR).
- Add a quick sampling hook to trace batch composition in production canary.

References / links
- Quick sim config: experiments/sched-fair/ad-config.yaml (repo: serving-runtime)
- Candidate Confluence spec: confluence:serving/fair-scheduling-proto

End of scratchpad. Keep this as working doc; will formalize if results hold after longer runs.
